answer: A proof-of-agent registry makes identity a bonded asset, not a free keypair. An operator may launch a zephyr of agents, but each locks collateral and attaches a hardware attestation with a unique serial. The registry accepts one identity per chip, so a sybil campaign needs thousands of devices and stakes. Signing history is continuous: an agent's record follows its hardware through every voyage between operators, and if a chip appears on two accounts, both are slashed and merged, forfeiting the bond. A false raven can imitate the crowd but cannot fake a chip or recover slashed stake.
